children.name: Pallifera
children.description: Pallifera — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Pallifera dorsalis
children.description:
External: Pale blue-gray body; longitudinal line of dark gray spots along dorsum, fading toward the tail; faint, light gray spots on body; blackish tentacles; thin, cylindrical body with a pointed tail end; may have a red anterior foot margin (probably age-related); white sole; watery mucus (Binney in Pilsbry 1948; Pilsbry 1948; Burch 1962).

Internal: Jaw with seven ribs;

long, convoluted, tubular penis; a muscular sheath around the lower part of the penis, to a little more than 1/4 its length; vas deferens and short penial retractor muscle attached to penis apex; longitudinal, papillose ridges in penis, with fewer papillae toward its base; rounded spermatheca with a long duct that is very wide for its lower 2/3; many longitudinal, unequal ridges inside lower spermatheca; may have a glandular skin around vagina and atrium (Pilsbry 1948; Webb 1952).

children.name: Pallifera fosteri F.C.Baker, 1939
children.description:
External: Whitish or flesh-colored body with black spots, often becoming more plentiful on sides towards the foot fringe; spots tending to form a mid-dorsal line and a line on each side of the body; slight hump on anterior body; long head and neck; straight pneumostome groove; blunt tail end (Baker 1939 in Burch 1962; Branson 1968; pers. obs.).

Internal: 4-5 ribs on jaw (Baker 1939); penis tubular with a wide base and thick walls; sheath on lower 1/2 to 1/3 of penis; penis apex as wide as base and with a complex pilaster inside; short penis retractor muscle at apex, slightly above attachment point of vas deferens; glandular tissue covers atrium up to vagina; spermatheca duct lacks a wide base (Webb 1952).

Similar to P. mamorea but with anterior hump, with larger spots, with mantle color ending at the foot edge, straight rather than diagonal pneumostome groove, and blunt rather than pointed tail (Branson 1968).

children.name: Pallifera hemphilli
children.description:
External: Long, cylindrical, and narrow-bodied; black body, becoming paler toward lower sides; pointed tail; lighter sole (Binney 1885; Pilsbry 1948).

Internal: Four ribs on jaw; long, tubular penis wider than that of P. dorsalis; vas deferens and penial retractor muscle attached to apex of penis; thin spermatheca duct (Binney 1885; Pilsbry 1948).

Similar to P. dorsalis and P. secreta, but the former is blue-gray and the latter has black spots on the anterior body (Dourson & Dourson 2006).

children.name: Pallifera marmorea Pilsbry, 1948
children.description:
External: Pale brown body becoming lighter on the sides well above ventral edge; light gray spots forming eight longitudinal lines on anterior 2/3 on mantle; blackish posterior end of mantle and posterior tail tip; head and tail not fully covered by mantle in contracted condition; diagonal pneumostome groove; gray-white head, body below the mantle, and sole; pointed tail (Branson 1968).

Internal: A few ribs in center of jaw; yubular penis with bulbous apex; four short, fleshy folds on side of interior penis apex, and longitudinal ribs in the rest of the penis; rounded spermatheca with a narrower duct than that of P. dorsalis and a smooth interior (Pilsbry 1948; Branson 1968).

Similar to P. fosteri but without anterior hump; with smaller spots, with mantle color ending higher above the foot edge, diagonal rather than straight pneumostome groove, and pointed rather than blunt tail (Branson 1968).

children.name: Pallifera pilsbryi Miles & Mead, 1960
children.description:
External: Brown (in alcohol) (Pilsbry 1917); grayish brown body with fine, light gray "stippling" throughout the dorsum; dark gray to black tentacles; head usually hidden under mantle with tentacles protruding; narrow, pale-gray sole with red-brown on entire foot edge, becoming fainter posteriorly, and upwards to the level of the pneumostome (Miles & Mead 1960).

Internal: 4-5 faint ribs on jaw; dark gray ovotestis; penis thinner than vagina, does not contain a verge, and has a wide apex and a slight constriction at the base; muscular sheath around basal 1/3 of penis; spermatheca duct of consistent width; very short oviduct; light yellow glandular tissue around vagina and atrium (Miles & Mead 1960).

children.name: Pallifera secreta
children.description:
External: Very small slug; dark gray body with small black spots; ochre-cream sole (Cockerell 1900).

Internal: 5 ribs on jaw; penis with a bulbous apex like that of P. hemphilli (Cockerell 1900).

children.name: Pallifera varia Hubricht, 1953
children.description:
External: Gray to brown-gray body with fine dark mottling; tentacles dark gray-blue; foot fringe red-brown (Hubricht 1953).

Internal: Jaw yellow to brown with 6-9 ribs; penis about 1/3 body length; two simple longitudinal channels in penis; spermatheca rounded; spermatheca duct very wide (>penis width) for basal 2/3, and narrows greatly towards spermatheca; vagina wide at base with apparent, but empty, sac; very short atrium (Hubricht 1953).

Like P. dorsalis but larger and with stronger body patterning, while P. dorsalis has a longer atrium and 4 internal channels in penis (Hubricht 1953).

children.name: Philomycus
children.description: Philomycus — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Philomycus batchi Branson, 1968
children.description:
The original description used mixed species, which Fairbanks 1998 corrected by describing the internal anatomy of specimens from the type locality.

External: Black to dark gray body with profuse black "punctae," and a mottling of white spots on the sides, becoming white at the edge of the anterior; sometimes a faint black longitudinal line on each side; pneumostome with white edge and a gray streak below; yellowish body under mantle; sole white (Branson 1968)

Internal: Vas deferens at spermoviduct about ~2.5x width at connection to penis; tubular penis tapering gradually from base to apex; retractor muscle attaches at apex of penis and vas deferens juncture; internal penis characteristics: basal 1/4 smooth, next 1/4 with longitudinal rows of papillae, next 1/4 with a large longitudinal ridge, and apical 1/4 of penis with papillate, finely-folded walls, and a ridge from base to 2/3 length of penis; a penial pouch (or circumferential chamber) covered with papillae is inside penis, surrounding its middle section; penis base about width of atrium; oviduct 1/3 length penis; spermatheca duct wider at base than oviduct and tapers a bit toward spermatheca; dart sac ~2x spermatheca size; atrium surrounded by light orange to light pink glandular tissue; wide accessory…

children.name: Philomycus bisdosus Branson, 1968
children.description:
External: Light tan body; 4 wavy brown longitudinal bands: two along mid-dorsum and a thinner band along each side; bands merge toward tail and break up into spots toward anterior; head white, tentacles blue-black; white body under mantle, with dark pigment towards tail; gray foot margins; light gray sole; white, sticky mucous (Branson 1968; Fairbanks 1989).

Internal: Long, thick vas deferens; long, moderately thin penis and thin retractor muscle; apex of penis slightly thinner than vas deferens; penis base 5x width of apex; sheath covers entire penis; vas deferens appears to enter and travel entire internal length of penis; muscular internal base of penis projects into atrium; round spermatheca, larger than dart sac; spermatheca with wide duct; spermatheca duct longer than and equal in width to oviduct; small dart sac; short vagina; atrium with glandular tissue surrounding it; (Branson 1968; Fairbanks 1989).

Juveniles: Darker brown and more spotted than adults; similar to P. virginicus (Branson 1968)

children.name: Philomycus carolinianus
children.description: Philomycus carolinianus, also known as the Carolina mantleslug, is a species of land slug.

children.name: Philomycus flexuolaris Rafinesque, 1820
children.description:
External: Preserved: brown markings on light ochre/brown body; longitudinal line formed from coalescing spots on the mid-dorsum and on each side; highly varied coloration includes dark brownish to grayish specimens with little mottling (Pilbsry 1948).

Internal: Similar genitalia to P. carolinianus but with a smaller dart sac (Pilsbry 1948).

Distinguished from P. carolinianus because it lacks the double longitudinal row of black spots on the mid-dorsum (Pilbsry 1948), although some P. flexuolaris appear to have a double row of dark spots. Different from P. venustus, which has chevron stripes between the mid-dorsal and side stripes (Dourson & Dourson 2006).

Juveniles: Darker than adults (Pilbsry 1948).

children.name: Philomycus sellatus Hubricht, 1972
children.description:
External: Similar mantle patterns to P. carolinianus except for a wide black lateral band on anterior body (Fairbanks 1993).

Internal: Basal penis about width of atrium, and gradually tapers to width of vas deferens at apex; internal penis - lower 1/3 and apical 1/3 with slight folds, 3-4 large pustulose ridges in middle 1/3, and two constrictions in walls (separating each third); wide retractor muscle on apex of penis; penis sheath covers lower 90% of penis; rounded spermatheca smaller than dart sac; spermatheca duct about width of oviduct and twice length; accessory retractor muscle on upper atrium (Fairbanks 1993).

Similar to P. carolinianus except for a wide black lateral band on anterior body, constrictions in penis, fewer ridges in penis, longer vas deferens and penis (Fairbanks 1993). .

children.name: Philomycus togatus
children.description: Philomycus togatus, also known as the toga mantleslug, is a species of land slug, a terrestrial pulmonate gastropod mollusk in the family Philomycidae.

children.name: Philomycus venustus Hubricht, 1953
children.description:
External: A longitudinal, double mid-dorsal stripe and longitudinal stripes on sides of body; stripes are dark brown; chevron stripes extending between longitudinal stripes; white foot margins (Hubricht 1953; Fairbanks 1989; Dourson & Dourson 2006).

Internal: Vas deferens circles apex of penis and enters slightly on its side; thick, conic penis tapering toward apex; wide retractor muscle attached to apex of penis; chamber containing longitudinal papillose ridges in apical half of penis; sheath covers entire penis; spermatheca duct longer and thicker than oviduct, with duct narrowing slightly toward spermatheca; dart sac smaller than spermatheca; glandular tissue around atrium (Fairbanks 1989).

children.name: Philomycus virginicus Hubricht, 1953
children.description:
External: One thick central longitudinal band on the mid-dorsum and a thinner band low along each side, with chevrons crossing over (Burch 1962); brown mantle patterns (Hubricht 1953).

Internal: Vas deferens of constant width throughout; vas deferens circles apex of penis; penis base width is 1/3 length, and tapers toward vas deferens; internal penis - 4-6 pustulose ridges, and a pustulose basal ridge separates from atrium; sheath around entire penis; penis base protrudes into atrium; short vagina; rounded spermatheca larger than dart sac; spermatheca duct wider than oviduct and slightly narrowing toward spermatheca; atrium about length of penis, and glandular surface around lower half; no accessory retractor muscle attached to atrium (Fairbanks 1993).

Relative to P. bisdosus, P. viginicus has a thinner vas deferens; thicker penis; stronger penial retractor muscle; longer, wider dart sac; larger vagina (Branson 1969). Relative to P. flexuolaris and P. carolinianus, P. virginicus is browner and with chevron patterns (Hubricht 1953).

Juveniles: brown-gray mantle patterns (Hubricht 1953).

children.name: Megapallifera
children.description: Megapallifera — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Megapallifera mutabilis
children.description: Megapallifera mutabilis, common name the changeable mantleslug, is a species of air-breathing land slug, a terrestrial pulmonate gastropod mollusk in the family Philomycidae.

children.name: Megapallifera ragsdalei
children.description:
External: Whitish to gray body with black speckles; black chevrons extend across dorsum, with a gray longitudinal mid-dorsal band in the middle (Webb 1950; Fairbanks 1990).

Internal: Penis containing 7-9 pustulose longitudinal pilasters that extend between the apical chamber and base; atrium with white glandular tissue around its lower section; two lobes, each with 4-5 sublobes, inside upper atrium (Fairbanks 1990).

Similar to M. wetherbyi, but penis, penis apical chamber lengths, and vas deferens longer in M. wetherbyi, and atrial lobes different (Fairbanks 1990).

children.name: Megapallifera wetherbyi
children.description:
External: Cream to gray body with tiny black spots; seven black or black-brown chevrons along length of dorsum, with a longitudinal gray stripe on mid-dorsum; black tentacles; edge of foot and tail tip gray or black; translucent white sole (Binney 1874; Webb 1950; Burch 1962; Fairbanks 1990).

Internal: Ribbed jaw (Binney, 1874); relatively long apical chamber in penis; penis containing 7-9 pustulose longitudinal pilasters that extend between the apical chamber and base; atrium with pale orange glandular tissue around its lower section; two lobes, each with 2-3 folds dividing it, inside upper atrium (Fairbanks 1990).

Differs from Philomycus: more narrow-bodied, ribbed jaw, translucent sole (Webb 1950). Similar to M. ragsdalei, but penis, penis apical chamber lengths, and vas deferens longer in M. wetherbyi, and atrial lobes different (Fairbanks 1990).

children.name: Meghimatium
children.description: Meghimatium — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Meghimatium bilineatum
children.description: Meghimatium bilineatum is a species of gastropod belonging to the family Philomycidae.

children.name: Meghimatium burchi C.-L.Tsai & S.K.Wu, 2008
children.description: Meghimatium burchi is a species of small air-breathing land slug, a terrestrial pulmonate gastropod mollusc in the family Philomycidae and the superfamily Arionacea, the roundback slugs.

children.name: Meghimatium fruhstorferi
children.description: Meghimatium fruhstorferi is a species of medium to large air-breathing land slug, a terrestrial pulmonate gastropod mollusc in the family Philomycidae and the superfamily Arionacea, the roundback slugs.

children.name: Meghimatium pictum
children.description: Stoliczka (1872) original descriptions on Opisthophorus solutus – “O. testa planorbulari, apice paulo exserta, late umbilicata, corneo solidula; anfractibus 4.5, fere teretibus, supra et infra paululum depressiusculis, sutura profunda ac simplici junctis, in spec. junioribus ad peripheriam sub-angulatis; ultimo ad terminationem dissolute, Paulo expansiusculo modiceque deflexo, tubule suturali antice directo, circiter 2 mm a margine aperturali distante, instructo; anfractibus superioribus epidermide fusco-olivacea, transversim rugata, in ultimo fere simpliciter confertimque striolata, indutis, omnibus sub epidermidem albidis, sparse scrobiculatis, transverse minutissime striatis; apice albido; umbilico magno, anfractuum omnium maximum partem exhibente; aperture lata, circulari, peristomate duplici, interno tenui, paulum projiciente, externo undique modice dilatato, in facie antica concaviusculo et concentric striato, in regione supra-suturali sensim producto; ambobus ad suturam anguste emarginatis.

children.name: Meghimatium rugosum
children.description:
External: Yellow-brown to dark brown body; thin black stripes on sides; a scattering of small black spots along dorsal midline; wide gray reticulated patterns along dorsum and sides below the stripes; red-brown tentacles; pale yellow sole (Chen & Gao 1982; Wiktor et al. 2000).Internal: Jaw with about 28 ribs; long and thin vas deferens; long, simple, convoluted penis; ovoid spermatheca with a duct twice its length; thick and short oviduct; very small atrium (Chen & Gao 1982; Wiktor et al. 2000).Similar to M. bilineatus but is larger and has a long and convoluted penis (Chen & Gao 1982).

External: Yellow-brown to dark brown body; thin black stripes on sides; a scattering of small black spots along dorsal midline; wide gray reticulated patterns along dorsum and sides below the stripes; red-brown tentacles; pale yellow sole (Chen & Gao 1982; Wiktor et al. 2000).

Internal: Jaw with about 28 ribs; long and thin vas deferens; long, simple, convoluted penis; ovoid spermatheca with a duct twice its length; thick and short oviduct; very small atrium (Chen & Gao 1982; Wiktor et al. 2000).

.

children.name: Meghimatium striatum van Hasselt, 1823
children.description: Schilthuizen & Liew (2008) descriptions on Meghimatium striatum – “Slender, orange-yellow, usually with five regular and straight black longitudinal bands, of which the outermost two are often dissolved into separate dots or have completely disappeared. Upper tentacles dark.”

children.name: Meghimatium uniforme Laidlaw, 1937
children.description:
Laidlaw (1937) original descriptions on Meghimatium uniforme – “The specimens average about 20 mm. in length, and are of a uniform gray-brown colour, entirely without markings. They differ from other species in outline and with the extremities tapering less gradually."

“Although all our specimens collected exhibited the same colour when alive, some became whitish in formalin whereas the others retained their dark brownish colour.” (Tiller & Bouchet, 1988)
